criticalAuthoringDetails: Chapter 2 number reference reaches Million and Milliarde. Teach the productive tens/hundreds/thousands pattern and recognize the large-number labels rather than silently limiting the chapter to 100.
Chapter 1 recap initially uses a subset of subject pronouns; chapter 2 supplies the complete person system and sein/haben paradigms.
Chapter 5 possesses a full possessor set, including unser, euer/eure and formal Ihr; the stated possessive case scope is nominative and accusative.
Chapter 6 includes war and hatte before the perfect, a full accusative-pronoun set, für plus accusative, and separable verbs both alone and with a modal.
Chapter 7 explicitly teaches doch as an affirmative contradiction of a negative question, dative plural noun n, and contractions zum, zur, beim, vom and im.
Chapter 8 must distinguish dürfen nicht from müssen; one expresses prohibition and the other obligation. Reported instructions use a new main clause with sollen, not an untaught dass clause.

Chapter 9 explicitly contrasts in plus accusative destination with in plus dative location. All nine two-way prepositions occur in the scope, especially for static dative location; do not infer that the supplied summaries teach full productive accusative placement with every one of them.
Chapter 10 includes regular, irregular and ieren participles and the sein exceptions bleiben and passieren. The recap recommends ordinary war/hatte instead of routinely using bin gewesen/habe gehabt.
Chapter 11 welcher and dieser tables include dative as well as nominative and accusative. Its dative verbs are gefallen, stehen, passen and helfen; noun-subject agreement still matters.
Chapter 11 distinguishes stressed separable prefixes and unstressed inseparable prefixes, and their different placement of ge in the perfect.
Chapter 12 temporal prepositions include ab, an, in, nach, seit and vor. Its question-word system includes person case forms wer/wen/wem; the appendix adds quantity wie viel/wie viele.
The appendix gives full present paradigms for werden and wissen; reference lookup must support these even though they are not main TOC grammar headings.
TOC headings for pronunciation, learning strategies and cultural contexts are substantive syllabus outcomes, not optional objective labels.
Platform reviews add mixed-task transfer, polite versus unfriendly instruction delivery, brief absence messages, mediated retelling, regional food and multilingual D-A-CH contexts.
Contextual readings may contain incidental grammar beyond their main lesson targets. Their presence does not make every incidental construction a required new A1 grammar explanation.

a1FunctionalCrosscheck.interpretation: The checks below paraphrase broad A1 capabilities. They are not a mandated German grammar syllabus or an exam guarantee. Findings concern summary scope; current app lessons were not evaluated.

checks.goal: Recognize basic personal, family and nearby-environment language in slow clear speech.
checks.neededVerification: Use unseen short recordings with names, numbers and key details.

checks.goal: Understand familiar words and simple sentences on everyday notices or displays.
checks.status: scope present; varied notice reading needs verification
checks.neededVerification: Include an original sign, directory or short notice task.

checks.goal: Exchange familiar personal information and immediate needs with help or repetition.
checks.neededVerification: Practice a two-way exchange plus an unclear detail requiring repair.

checks.goal: Describe familiar people and where one lives in simple phrases.
checks.neededVerification: Give a short home or family description without copying.

checks.goal: Write a basic postcard and enter personal details into a form.
checks.status: scope present; form completion is easy to omit in a sentence-only app
checks.neededVerification: Require an original multi-field personal form and postcard.

supplementCandidates.title: Request slower speech or simpler wording in addition to repetition and spelling.
supplementCandidates.basis: Explicit repair set in chapter 10 covers repeating and spelling; slower delivery and rephrasing are not explicit in the inspected chapter summaries.

supplementCandidates.title: Interpret simple public signs and opening-hour notices across several settings.
supplementCandidates.basis: Directory scanning and housing ads are explicit; an independent set of ordinary public notices is not explicit in the inspected summaries.

supplementCandidates.title: Carry out a basic accommodation check-in or booking and a simple ticket purchase.
supplementCandidates.basis: Travel, routes, forms and shopping supply reusable language; these complete service transactions are not named in the inspected summary scope. Treat them as practical transfer extensions rather than a CEFR-mandated topic list.

supplementCandidates.title: Ask for simple immediate practical help and state a basic problem.
supplementCandidates.basis: Doctor and shopping requests are explicit, but lost items and a concise help request are not explicit in the inspected summaries.

uncertainties: No claim is made that every chapter exercise, video, recording or alphabetical vocabulary entry was inspected. This is a finite summary-grounded audit.
No original audio was heard. Pronunciation topics are verified as source headings; discrimination and production ability remain untested.

The scope of the chapter-cultural readings is verified from the TOC; precise narrative details beyond recap and platform pages should be checked against the relevant chapter page before being authored as source facts.
Keywords are semantic anchors and representative finite sets, not a complete extraction of the book word list or every inflected form.
Supplement candidates indicate tasks not explicit in the inspected summary sources; they do not prove the book lacks such language elsewhere.
No lesson IDs, coverage percentages or mastered statuses are assigned. Explicit lesson mapping and independent transfer assessment are separate work.
